reconstructed_theorem_text:
For every complete real inner-product space E (with its normed additive commutative group structure), every function f:E→ℝ, and every real β and h, assume: f is continuously Fréchet differentiable on all of E; f is convex on all of E, meaning f((1-t)x+t y)≤(1-t)f(x)+t f(y) for all x,y∈E and t∈[0,1]; h>0; βh≤1; and for every x,y∈E,
f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y-x⟩+(β/2)‖y-x‖².
Here ∇f is the Riesz gradient. Then for every initial point x₀∈E, every comparator z∈E, and every natural number N>0, define the actual iterates by xₖ₊₁=xₖ-h∇f(xₖ). The theorem gives the last-iterate bound
f(x_N)-f(z)≤‖x₀-z‖²/(2hN).
The same fixed step h is used at each iteration, and the norm and inner product are those of E. There is no finite-dimensionality assumption, explicit positive or nonnegative sign assumption on β, or assumption that z is a minimizer, stationary point, or selected comparator; both x₀ and z are universally quantified. No existence of a minimizer, gradient Lipschitz condition, or additional convergence conclusion is asserted. N=0 and h=0 are excluded, so the displayed denominator is strictly positive. If x₀=z, the displayed right side is zero. There are no conditional conclusion branches.
